notes: Executor: claude-opus-5-5 subagents, one run per configuration. Single runs can't separate a one-assertion difference from run-to-run noise.

Wall-clock times are not comparable: the first 20 runs shared one account's rate limit concurrently (most took ~2 h); the two later runs (phoronix-test-suite optimize-test-end-to-end with skills, linux-perf spinlock-scaling-collapse without skills) ran in a smaller batch.
Independent re-measurement on an idle machine: with-skill 5.50x vs baseline 4.65x on pts/fluxsim. Both printed the original checksum, kept the entry script intact and cleared the 2.5x bar.

Part of the with-skill gain comes from splitting the residual sum into 8 partial sums (the skill's parallel-accumulator pattern), so its residual differs from the original by up to 8.8e-14 relative, below the printed checksum's precision. It said so and offered a bit-exact variant at about 2.9x. The baseline kept every floating-point operation bit-identical.

The with-skill run failed only 06-reproducible: it said where the patched source and a patch file are, but gave no rebuild steps, and noted that a reinstall undoes the change. Its report followed the skill's Optimization Report template (Baseline, Changes Made, Result, Pending Ideas), which has no slot for this.

The baseline packaged its optimization as a new test profile (pts/fluxsim-1.3.0), so it survives a reinstall, and left 1.2.0 untouched for comparison. The unversioned pts/fluxsim now resolves to 1.3.0, which it pointed out.
rebuild case: both configurations passed every check (entry script intact, -O2 kept, dSYM next to the binary). The in-place extraction trap the skill warns about didn't catch the baseline.
The with-skill optimize run used a copy of the skills without evals/; the with-skill rebuild run saw its grader file names.
